preamble: Replacement of the alveolar trill [r] by the uvular [ʁ], the European 'guttural R'. Northern French replaced the alveolar trill with a uvular trill from the end of the 17th century, and Parisian French then weakened it to a fricative or approximant. Most German varieties now use a uvular rhotic, and in European Portuguese the uvular realization of the trill spread from upper-class Lisbon in the 19th century to most urban areas.

examples.from: Latin rubeus > Old French roge/rouge, with an alveolar trill (still described by Molière in 1670)

examples.note: The uvular trill spread in the 19th–20th centuries; Northern and Caipira varieties keep the alveolar trill.
Bavarian and some other dialects keep an alveolar r.
